newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures close lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures close lower.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended lower amid profit-taking and minor technical weakness.

Morning trade was directionless and afternoon action weak as players sought to find their footing after a recent run to record highs. Some said the market was a bit overbought but that any pullbacks were attracting buyers.
June Standard and Poor's 500 futures slipped below Wednesday's session low of 844.60, but left support at 843.00 and Tuesday's 842.60 low intact.
The June S&P 500 record high was set Tuesday at 854.70.
Several traders deemed the day's activity consolidation.
"It's probably doing what it should be doing" after recent gains, an S&P 500 futures trader said.
He and other traders called action overall only light to moderate as local players dominated trade much of the day.
"Basically the floor is the one that pushed it, but we just couldn't get any follow-through through yesterday's lows," the trader said.
June S&Ps fell below Wednesday's 844.60 low and triggered small sell stops, but stalled at 844.00 before rebounding slightly into the close, traders said.
Traders kept a close eye on firm June Treasury bond futures, which strengthened all afternoon.
Treasury's auction of $12 billion five-year notes saw favorable results, pushing June T-bonds to 109-11/32. A high yield of 6.616 percent was produced from the auction.

At the close, June S&P 500s were down 5.05 points at 845.50, Nasdaq 100 crumbled 11.35 points to 973.65, NYSE Composites were down 1.95 at 439.35, KCBT Value Lines fell 1.55 to 751.85, Nikkeis were down 45 at 20,300, Midcap 400s were down 0.95 at 276.85, and Russell 2000s were down 1.20 at 378.70. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
